key_insight: A parameter-free ab initio framework can predict charge transport in molecular semiconductors by simulating full electron–phonon dynamics, revealing transport regimes and bottlenecks from first principles.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable material screening and device design for organic transistors and photovoltaics by linking atomic structure directly to mobility and conductivity.
method: Compute electron–phonon Hamiltonians from first principles.
Propagate carriers over hundreds-of-molecule domains with the full phonon spectrum.
Use nonperturbative Green–Kubo dynamics so transport mechanisms emerge without assuming a specific hopping or band model.
evidence_signal: Across five representative crystals, the framework reproduces measured mobilities, temperature exponents, and optical-conductivity fingerprints.
watch_item: The approach is computationally demanding and depends on high-quality ab initio electron–phonon calculations, which may limit routine use for very large or complex systems.
paper_title: First-Principles Origins of Charge Transport in Molecular Semiconductors
